movements.name: Hip hinge drill
cues: Stand a foot from a wall
Push hips back to touch it
Shins stay nearly vertical
Flat back, chest proud

movements.name: Cossack squat
cues: Wide stance
Sit into one hip, other leg straight with toes up
Heel down
Stay tall

movements.name: Monk squat
cues: Deep squat, palms together
Elbows push knees out
Chest up
Breathe

movements.name: Reverse lunge
cues: Step back long
Back knee hovers
Front shin vertical
Drive through the front heel

movements.name: Hindu push-up
cues: Start in downward dog
Swoop chest low and forward into upward dog
Push back to downward dog

movements.name: Step-back burpee
cues: Hands down
Step back one foot at a time
Step in, stand
No jump

movements.name: Deep squat hold
cues: Heels down
Hold the 18 goblet-style as a counterweight, or hold a door frame
Breathe

movements.name: Lizard twist
cues: Deep lunge, back knee down
Hand inside the front foot
Rotate and reach the other arm to the sky

movements.name: Pump stretch
cues: Flow from downward dog to plank and back
From the knees at first

movements.name: Straddle
cues: Sit tall, legs wide, knees soft
Hinge forward from the hips, not the back

movements.name: Bridge (regressed)
cues: Glute bridge hold
Then tabletop / crab hold
Then hands on the couch
Full wheel later

movements.name: Deep twist squat
cues: Sit into a deep squat, heels down
One hand to the floor, reach the other arm to the sky
Twist side to side slowly
Hold a door frame if balance is shaky

movements.name: Downward dog pulses
cues: Hands and feet down, hips high
Gently pulse the heels toward the floor
Bent knees are fine; keep the back long

movements.name: Pigeon pose
cues: Front shin across, back leg long behind
Hips square, sink them toward the floor
Cushion under the front hip if it doesn't reach
Ease off if the front knee hurts

movements.name: Couch stretch
cues: Kneel facing away from a wall or couch, cushion under the back knee
Back shin up the wall or couch, front foot flat ahead
Squeeze the back glute and tuck the hips under before you rise
Rise only as tall as you can without arching the lower back
Too strong? Move the back knee farther from the wall
Ease off if the knee hurts

movements.name: Frog pose
cues: On forearms and knees, knees wide
Ankles in line with the knees
Ease the hips back and down
Pad under the knees

movements.name: Cobra
cues: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders
Press up; hips stay on the floor
Shoulders down, away from the ears
Only as high as the lower back likes

movements.name: Reverse prayer pose
cues: Hands behind your back, palms together, fingers pointing up
Roll the shoulders back and open the chest
Palms won't meet? Hold opposite elbows instead
Ease the hands lower if the wrists complain

movements.name: Seated spinal twist
cues: Sit tall; plant one foot outside the other knee
Turn toward the raised knee; hook the opposite elbow outside it
Back hand on the floor behind you
Breathe in to sit taller, breathe out to twist deeper

movements.name: Lying spinal twist
cues: Lie on your back, arms out wide in a T
Hug one knee to your chest; the other leg stays long
Let the bent knee drop across your body to the side the timer says
Both shoulders stay heavy on the floor; look the other way if your neck likes it
Knee doesn't reach the floor? Rest it on a cushion
Don't push the knee down; breathe out and let it sink

movements.name: Morning routine (10 moves)
cues: Jumping twists, arm circles, arm swings, elbow throws, ragdoll twists
Body waves, side bends, lunge reaches, monk squats, Cossack squats
30 s each, done continuously

movements.name: Air squat
cues: Feet shoulder-width
Sit between the heels
Chest up, heels down

movements.name: Prisoner squat
cues: Hands behind the head, elbows wide
Sit between the heels
Chest up

movements.name: Push-up
cues: Hands under shoulders
Body in one straight line
Knees or hands on a bench is fine

movements.name: Plank
cues: Elbows under shoulders
Squeeze glutes
Ribs down, breathe

movements.name: Dead hang
cues: Full grip on the bar
Let the shoulders open gently
Feet can touch the floor to start

movements.name: Burpee
movements.unlockNote: Locked until knees are pain-free at full Savage volume

movements.name: Jump squat
movements.unlockNote: Locked until knees are pain-free at full Savage volume

movements.name: Split jump
movements.unlockNote: Locked until knees are pain-free at full Savage volume

movements.name: Deadlift
cues: Bell between the arches
Hips back, flat back
Lats tight
Stand by squeezing the glutes

movements.name: Goblet squat
cues: Hold by the horns at chest
Elbows inside knees
Sit between the heels
Chest up

movements.name: Single-arm press
cues: Rack position, wrist straight
Squeeze glutes
Press up and slightly out; biceps by ear
Lower with control

movements.name: Bent-over row
cues: Hinge, flat back
Pull elbow to hip
Don't twist
Pause at the top

movements.name: Floor press
cues: Lying, elbow on the floor at ~45°
Press straight up
Wrist stacked over elbow

movements.name: Halo
cues: Horns grip, bell upside down
Circle tight around the head
Ribs down, glutes tight

movements.name: Suitcase carry
cues: Bell at your side
Shoulders level
Walk tall, don't lean

movements.name: Single-leg deadlift
cues: Soft standing knee
Hips square
Back leg and torso move as one
Reach the bell toward the floor

movements.name: Pullover
cues: Lying, bell held by the horns
Lower behind the head slowly
Ribs stay down

movements.name: Arm bar
cues: Lying, bell locked out overhead
Roll to your side
Eyes on the bell
Shoulder packed

movements.name: Get-up (in pieces)
cues: Roll to elbow → hand → high bridge → kneel → stand
Eyes on the bell
Arm locked

movements.name: Mini-flow: halo → goblet squat → halo
cues: Slow and smooth, no rushing the transitions
Halo: ribs down, glutes tight
Squat: elbows inside knees, chest up

movements.name: Suitcase deadlift
cues: Bell beside one foot
Hinge straight down
Don't let the torso tilt

movements.name: Rack squat (single-hand squat)
cues: Bell in rack position
Same squat cues as the goblet squat
Resist leaning to the bell side

movements.name: Bottoms-up press
cues: Bell upside down
Crush grip
Slow, strict press

movements.name: Standing push-out
cues: Stand tall, feet hip-width; hold the bell by the horns against your chest
Squeeze the horns hard; ribs down, glutes tight
Breathe out and push the bell straight out at chest height until your arms are straight
Pause 1–2 s; don't lean back or shrug
Bring it back to your chest slowly

movements.name: Horn push-up
cues: Hands on the bell's horns, body in a straight plank
Lower the chest toward the handle, elbows at about 45 degrees
Press up; brace so the bell doesn't wobble

movements.name: Glute bridge
cues: Lie on your back, feet flat, the bell resting on your hips
Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes to lift the hips
Pause at the top with ribs down, then lower slowly

movements.name: Loaded reverse lunge
cues: Hold the bell goblet-style or in the rack
Step back and lower the back knee softly toward the floor
Push through the front heel to stand tall

movements.name: Plank pull-through
cues: High plank, feet wide, the bell beside you
Reach under with the far hand and drag the bell across
Keep the hips square and still; switch hands each rep

movements.name: Rack hold
cues: Bring the bell to the rack: on the forearm, against the chest
Wrist straight, elbow tucked, stand tall
Breathe and brace; don't lean away from the bell

movements.name: Overhead carry
cues: Press the bell overhead, arm locked, biceps by the ear
Walk tall with ribs down and slow steps
Switch arms each set

movements.name: Supported row (hand on thigh)
cues: Staggered stance, hinge forward, flat back
Brace the free hand on the front thigh
Pull the elbow to the hip; pause at the top
Easier version of the bent-over row

movements.name: Tactical crossover
cues: Wide stance, hinged, flat back; bell on the floor outside one foot
Row it to your belly with the near hand
Pass it to the other hand in the middle; lower it outside the other foot
Pull with the elbow, not the lower back; don't twist
Each pass is one rep

movements.name: Front-to-back raise
cues: Bell upside down by the horns, in front of your face
Press it overhead, then bend the elbows and lower it behind the head
Reverse over the top back to the front
Ribs down, glutes tight: no arching the lower back
Elbows point forward behind the head; slow

movements.name: Curl → shoulder press
cues: Bell hanging in front of the thigh: one hand on the handle, or both on the horns
Curl it to the chest, no swinging
Press overhead, biceps by the ear; glutes tight
Lower to the chest, then uncurl
One hand: same reps each side

movements.name: Side → front raise
cues: Bell by the horns in front of the hips
Sweep it out and up to one side to shoulder height, then back
Raise it straight in front up to overhead, then back
Side + front = one rep; switch sides on each side raise
Elbows slightly bent, no leaning back; slow

movements.name: Pullover → side pull
cues: Bell by the horns behind the head, elbows up
Bring it over the top and down to the hips; ribs down
One hand on the handle: pull it up close along your side to shoulder height, elbow above the hand
Lower it and return it behind the head; switch sides each rep

movements.name: Hammer curl
cues: Bell by your side, palm facing in
Curl to the shoulder
Upper arm stays still at your side; no hip swing
Lower over 2–3 s

movements.name: Curl → pullover
cues: Both hands on the horns, bell in front of the hips
Curl to the chest, no momentum
Raise it overhead and lower it behind the head
Reverse over the top to the chest, then uncurl
Ribs down, glutes tight; elbows point forward behind the head

movements.name: Hand-to-hand curl
cues: Bell in one hand at the hip
Curl it to the chest
Pass it to the other hand at the top; lower it with that hand
A controlled pass, not a toss (to start)
Upper arms stay at your sides

movements.name: Over-shoulder pull
cues: Bell in one hand at the hip
Curl it up and keep going: lift the elbow so the bell passes your face
It settles behind the same shoulder, hand near the forehead, elbow high
Reverse back down to the hip
Slow; keep it close to the head, don't let it drop

movements.name: Curl → goblet press
cues: Both hands on the horns, bell hanging at the hips
Curl it to the chest, no hip swing
Press it overhead, biceps by the ears
Lower to the chest, then uncurl to the hips
Glutes tight and ribs down on the press
Shoulder hold: curl to the chest + goblet squat, no press

movements.name: Hike pass
cues: Bell a foot in front
Tip it back and hike it high between the thighs, like a football snap
Set it down

movements.name: Full-stop swing (dead-stop)
cues: Park the bell on the floor between every rep
Hike, snap the hips, bell floats to chest height
Guide it back to the same spot and reset

movements.name: Two-hand swing
cues: Hinge, not squat
Snap hips and glutes; bell floats to chest height
Arms are ropes
Let it fall back between the thighs

movements.name: Single-arm swing
cues: Hike the bell back high between the legs with one hand
Snap the hips; the bell floats to chest height
Keep the shoulder down and back; the free arm swings along

movements.name: Hand-to-hand swing
cues: Swing like a two-hand swing, one hand on the bell
Switch hands at the top, when the bell feels weightless
Hips drive every rep; watch the bell when you switch

movements.name: Rotational swing
cues: Swing back, then turn the hips so the bell travels to one side
Pivot the back foot; the hips steer the bell
Do one side, then the other

movements.name: Side swing
cues: Savage swing: the bell travels outside the legs

movements.name: Lateral swing
cues: Savage swing: the bell travels outside the legs

movements.name: Clean
cues: Bell travels close
Hand punches through
Soft landing in the rack, no forearm bang

movements.name: Tactical clean
cues: Savage clean variant; see the program video

movements.name: High pull
cues: Swing back with one hand, then pull the elbow high and back at the top
Keep the bell close; the hand ends near the ear
The hips drive it; the arm only guides

movements.name: Ballistic row
cues: Hinge with a flat back, the bell hanging
Drive the bell up into a fast row, elbow to the hip
Let it drop back under control and go again

movements.name: Push press
cues: Leg-driven overhead: dip and drive

movements.name: Jerk
cues: Bell in the rack; a small dip with the knees
Drive up, then dip again under the bell as it rises
Lock out overhead, then stand tall

movements.name: Snatch
movements.unlockNote: Phase 4; needs a solid swing, high pull and clean
cues: Swing back, then pull the bell close, like a high pull
Punch the hand up through the handle so the bell lands softly on the forearm
Lock out overhead, then let it drop back between the legs

movements.name: Lawn mower starter
cues: Staggered stance, hinge, the bell by the front foot
Pull it up and back like starting a mower, turning the chest
Lower under control; do one side, then the other

movements.name: Gravedigger
cues: Wide stance, hips back, both hands on the handle, bell between the feet
Drive up with the legs and hips; lift the bell across the body and over one shoulder
Like a shovel of dirt over the shoulder, but the bell stays under control
Pivot the back foot; flat back at the bottom
Return between the feet; alternate sides

movements.name: Uppercut
cues: Athletic stance, bell in one hand at the hip
Dip, then turn the hips and drive the bell up across the body to face height
Elbow bent like a punch
Turn from the hips and feet, not the lower back
Control it back down to the hip

movements.name: Woodchop
cues: Both hands on the handle, bell up over one shoulder
Chop it down across the body to outside the opposite knee
Hips and feet turn together; chest stays up
Exhale on the chop; control the bottom
Return along the same line

movements.name: Gorilla swing
cues: Wider, lower stance than a normal swing, knees well bent
Both hands on the handle; hike it deep between the legs
Drive the hips; the bell floats to chest height
Stay low and wide the whole set; arms long and loose
Flat back at the bottom

movements.name: Over-shoulder toss
cues: Wide stance, hinged, both hands on the handle, bell between the feet
Drive the hips and lift it across the body to rest behind one shoulder, elbows high
Guide it there, don't throw it; pivot toward that shoulder
Back down between the legs; switch shoulders every rep
Flat back at the bottom
Shoulder hold: gravedigger, stopping at chest height

movements.name: Thruster
cues: Bell in the rack or goblet-style; squat deep
Drive up and use that push to press overhead
Bring it back down as you sink into the next squat

movements.name: Full get-up
cues: Arm locked straight up; eyes on the bell the whole way
Elbow, hand, hips up, sweep the leg back to a kneel, stand
Reverse the same steps slowly back to the floor

movements.name: Windmill
cues: Bell locked overhead; feet turned away from the bell side
Push the hip out toward the bell and fold down, eyes on the bell
Slide the free hand down the leg, then stand back up slowly

movements.name: Helicopter
cues: Both hands on the handle; circle the bell around your head
Keep the arms close to the head; the core keeps you still
Change direction each set

movements.name: Overhead squat
cues: Lock the bell overhead, arm straight up
Squat as deep as you can while the arm stays straight and the chest stays up
Stand up without the bell drifting forward

movements.name: Figure-8 (through the legs)
cues: Wide stance, slight squat, flat back
Pass the bell between the legs, hand to hand, around one leg, then the other
Keep it low and smooth

movements.name: Around-the-world
cues: Stand tall and pass the bell around your waist, hand to hand
Keep hips and shoulders square; let the arms do the work
Switch direction halfway through the set

movements.name: Side swing to rack
cues: Swing the bell out to the side, then bring it across
Tame the arc and catch it in the rack
Soft knees; do one side, then the other

movements.name: Side swing to snatch
cues: Swing the bell out to the side, then bring it across and up
Punch through like a snatch so it lands softly
Lock out overhead; come back down the same path

movements.name: Rotational clean
cues: Swing back and turn the hips toward the bell side
Pull the bell close and catch it in the rack as you turn back
The hips lead; the arm guides

movements.name: Cross-body clean
cues: Start with the bell outside the opposite foot
Pull it across the body and catch it in the rack
Keep it close; turn through the hips

movements.name: Devil's halo
cues: Hold the bell upside down by the horns, like a halo
Circle it behind the head, then down low through a deep squat
Smooth and slow; switch direction each set

movements.name: WTF / MFer
movements.unlockNote: Phase 3 (about Week 21+), with the 25. The MFer is the Advanced, higher-volume version
cues: Bell on the floor outside one foot; hinge, rotate down, grab with the near hand
Pull explosively; both hands catch it by the horns at the chest, bell upside down
Release one hand; lower to the floor outside the other foot; alternate
Pivot the feet; don't twist the lower back while bent under load

movements.name: Clean → squat
cues: Bell on the floor between the feet, both hands on the horns
Hinge and clean it to the chest, upside down: the hips drive it, not the arms
Full squat, elbows in, heels down
Stand, then lower the bell back to the floor

movements.name: Around-the-world → curl
cues: Bell in one hand at the hip
Pass it hand to hand around the waist, one full loop
Finish with one strict curl: that is one rep
Hips still; quick, clean switches behind the back
Change direction for the other side

movements.name: Clean → halo
cues: Bell between the feet, one hand on the handle
Hike it back and clean it to the rack; the hips drive it
Take it one-handed around the head in a tight halo, back to the rack
Lower it between the legs into the next rep; ribs down, bell close
Switch sides each rep, or each set
Shoulder hold: clean to a two-hand goblet hold, no halo

movements.name: Rotation pullover
cues: Bell upside down by the horns at the chest
Pivot the back foot and turn to one side, then back to the front
Raise it overhead and lower it behind the head; elbows point forward
Bring it back over to the chest, then turn to the other side
Ribs down, glutes tight overhead; turn from the feet and hips, never by twisting the lower back
Shoulder hold: just the turns, bell at the chest

movements.name: Alternating rotational clean
cues: Athletic stance, knees soft, one hand on the handle
Clean it to the chest as you turn the body to that side
Lower it, then clean it with the other hand, turning to that side
Alternate every rep; the hips drive each clean
Soft landing, no forearm bang; pivot the feet into each turn
Turn from the feet and hips, never by twisting the lower back

movements.name: Side toss → rotational snatch
cues: Athletic stance, knees soft, bell in one hand
Swing it out to one side, still holding the handle
Turn the other way and snatch it high overhead; the hips and feet change direction
Punch through so it lands softly; biceps by the ear
Lower back into the side swing; same reps each side
Shoulder hold: side swing only, no snatch

movements.name: Cross-body drop → rotational pull
cues: Athletic stance, knees soft, bell in one hand in front
Swing it across the body, down past the opposite hip
Pull it back the other way with a hard hip turn; the second hand meets the handle as it comes through
Reset to one hand; alternate the starting hand
Load the hips on the drop, explode on the pull; the arms guide, the hips power it
Turn from the feet and hips, never by twisting the lower back

movements.name: Held figure-8
cues: Athletic stance, knees soft, both hands on the bell, close to the body
Trace a figure-8 in front: down and across to one side, up through the middle, down to the other side
Turn the body under the bell and dip the knees each loop
Smooth, continuous loops; breathe
Turn from the feet and hips, never by twisting the lower back

movements.name: Extended figure-8 chop
cues: Both hands on the handle, arms long in front
Same figure-8 as the held one, but a bigger, chopping arc
Much harder on the shoulders and core: light and slow first
Don't let the bell pull you off balance
Turn from the feet and hips, never by twisting the lower back
Shoulder hold: held figure-8
